violations.requirement: ptr::copy requires src and dst to be valid for reads and writes of count*size_of::<T>() bytes. pointer::offset requires the result to stay in bounds of the same allocated object.
violations.explanation: drain is a safe pub fn and does not check that count <= self.offset. If count > self.offset, `self.offset - count` underflows. In release builds it wraps to a huge length. Then ptr::copy reads and writes far beyond the 16 KiB array, which is out-of-bounds and undefined behavior. If count > MAX_BUFFER_SIZE, `offset(count)` also goes past the end of the array allocation. Also, `offset` is a pub field, so it can be set larger than the array. Safe code can therefore trigger UB.
